chunks: And from him, from Ahmad ibn Sabih, from al-Husayn ibn Alwan, from Abdullah ibn al-Hasan, who said:

The Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) said: "The month of Ramadan ablates every fast, and the sacrifice (al-Nahr) ablates every slaughtered animal, and the alms-tax (al-Zakat) ablates every voluntary charity, and the ritual bath of major impurity (Ghusl al-Janabah) ablates every other bath."

key_terms.النَّحْرُ: The ritual sacrifice, specifically referring to the Eid al-Adha sacrifice or general ritual slaughter
key_terms.الْجَنَابَةِ: Major ritual impurity requiring a full body bath
key_terms.رَمَضَانَ: The month of Ramadan, the period of obligatory fasting
key_terms.نَسَخَ: Abated, superseded, or rendered null in terms of additional reward/obligation

ai.seo_question: What acts of worship are considered to abrogate or supersede other similar voluntary acts according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* articulates the principle of *naskh* (abrogation/preeminence) within the hierarchy of worship, establishing that obligatory acts supersede their voluntary counterparts. It specifically highlights Ramadan fasting, Eid al-Adha sacrifice, obligatory alms, and major ritual purification as the definitive standards that render other similar acts redundant or secondary. This reflects the Shia jurisprudential understanding that the performance of the primary duty fulfills the requirement for the general category, emphasizing the sufficiency of the obligatory act.
